Asobi Review 1.0 (build 1546) Oct 13, 2026

  • Reply to text written on the frame. Words typed on the picture with the Text tool are listed in the Notes sidebar, and now have a Reply field like any note, with the paperclip and the mic. The first reply gives the text its own thread, which goes to everyone in a review, to the report and to the exports. The words stay on the frame and are edited and removed there.
  • Input color space: remembered for the file, and Apply to All reaches every clip. A space you pick for a clip is now also remembered for that file on this Mac, so a Kitsu playlist opened again comes back with the QuickTime and the EXR each as you set them. Apply to All Movie Clips / Apply to All EXR Clips is in the Input picker itself, covers every timeline in the session, and sets the side of a clip that is off screen too: with the previews playing, it used to pass over the EXR behind each one.
  • Split at Playhead. One long event of a conformed cut that is two VFX shots: park on the frame that starts the second and choose Media ▸ Conformed Cut ▸ Split at Playhead. Each half is a shot of its own, with its own name and plate; select both and Join to undo.
  • The same take used again. A take that comes back later in a conformed cut is tagged Same take. Each shot gets its own plate by default; in Pull Plates, click PL01 on the later shot's row and choose Use that shot's Plate to write one plate for both.
  • Two takes in one shot. Events of different takes can be joined by hand into one shot (a split screen, a stitch between takes): it gets a plate for each take, PL01 then PL02 in the cut's order.
Earlier updates

1.0 (build 1476) Oct 12, 2026

  • DPX sequences play. 8, 10, 12 and 16-bit DPX files open and play like any other image sequence, read as the color space set for DPX in Settings, Color.
  • A tall floating Playlist with thumbnails could stop the app. Fixed.
  • Small fixes.

1.0 (build 1441) Oct 11, 2026

  • Network is in the Review menu. Review ▸ Network; it was under Window. It is also in the right-click Review menu.
  • A playlist on a network drive no longer slows the window. Whether each clip's file is there is checked in the background.
  • Locate Media… reads a folder in the background. A line above the toolbar says how far it has got.

  • A clip's input space sticks. A color space picked for a clip was lost the next time the clip came round whenever it differed from that file type's default; it now stays. Asobi Review 1.0 (build 1534) Oct 13, 2026

  • Zoom in on a Kitsu preview to see its source. A clip from Kitsu plays its preview movie; zoom in past 100% (and past what fits the window) and it switches to the source the Kitsu comment names, the EXR frames, then back to the preview when you zoom out. The source is looked for under the Kitsu source root, on the studio's projects drive and where Clip Locations has the clip, and a comment that names one frame stands for the whole sequence. In a shared review the switch stays a choice: Playback ▸ Source ▸ Flip to Source Media. Clip Locations now finds Kitsu-named originals by itself as it opens. Notes, marks and grade now follow a clip both ways across Flip to Source Media: a note made on the source is on the preview too.
  • Stop one plate, and try one again. While a pull runs, each plate being written or waiting has a small stop on its row: that plate stops and the pull goes on. A plate stopped part-way asks on its row: Keep (the next pull takes it up from the frames it has, in the same version) or Delete (the unfinished version goes; nothing finished is touched). Keep All and Delete All answer for all of them. A plate that failed gets Try Again, and Try Failed Again pulls only those. Taking a plate up from where it stopped applies to EXR and PNG plates Asobi writes itself; a plate from ARRI's tool or Resolve, or a QuickTime, is written again from its first frame.
  • Plates are written side by side. A pull now writes several plates at once: the ones Asobi writes itself as many as this Mac suits, with ARRI Reference Tool and DaVinci Resolve each writing one alongside. Settings ▸ Media ▸ Plates at once is Automatic (from this Mac's memory and cores, and it says what that comes to) or a number from 1 to 6. A pull from or to a network volume still writes one at a time unless you select Also on network volumes.
  • The Queue. A pull keeps being written whatever Pull Plates shows next, and a pull of another cut asked for meanwhile waits its turn behind it. Media ▸ Queue lists every pull: the one being written with each plate under way, the ones waiting, how the finished ones ended and what failed, and pulls an earlier run of Asobi left, with Resume. Stop All stops the lot.
